title: Put up thy sword
hookLine: friendship across divides, and deep caution about war
carry: peacemakers treat no one as an enemy

cards: Every election season, opposite yard signs go up on two neighboring lawns, and every season the two neighbors stop waving. They used to borrow each other's ladders.
Now they check the street before stepping outside so they won't have to talk. Nothing violent has happened. Nobody has done anything wrong, exactly.
But something between them has been switched off. Fratelli Tutti has a name for what was lost, and it's the second half of the letter's own subtitle: on fraternity and social friendship.
Today, that phrase, and where Francis follows it, all the way to the hardest place, war.

teach.b: First, what it means. Friendship is usually private: the few people you choose. Social friendship, for Francis, is the same warmth stretched across a whole society.
Not agreeing with everyone. Not even liking everyone. But refusing to treat anyone as an enemy by default, and staying at the table.
Second, how it's built. Francis puts dialogue at the center: approaching, listening, looking at each other, trying to understand, finding common ground.
He warns against the opposite, the feverish exchange of opinions online, where people talk past each other and only hear their own side.
Real dialogue, he says, is slow, and it costs something.
Third, the hard edge: war. The Catechism keeps the Church's long teaching that a nation may defend itself under strict conditions, the teaching called just war.
Francis doesn't erase it, but he says that with today's weapons it's very hard to meet those old criteria, and he cries out: never again war.
Some Catholics read this as a turn toward nonviolence; others read it as a warning within the old teaching. Both look to the same Gospel.
Jesus says, in the Douay-Rheims: "Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God."

And on the night he's arrested, when a disciple draws a sword, Jesus says: "Put up again thy sword into its place." Fourth, the link. Put side by side, war looks like social friendship failing at the largest scale.
Peace between nations starts small, with two neighbors and a ladder.

how: Catholics take up Fratelli Tutti's call to social friendship through parish dialogue groups, interfaith and community gatherings, and peace work; Catholic teaching on war is set out in the Catechism, and Francis's caution about it is discussed alongside that teaching.

games.q: Jesus is being arrested. one of his disciples draws a sword and strikes. what does Jesus say?
o: put up again thy sword into its place.
games.why: he tells him to put the sword away. Francis leans on moments like this when he urges deep caution about war.

practice: Bring to mind someone you've drifted from over a difference, politics, faith, family history, a side taken in an argument, and don't rehearse the argument; remember instead one thing about them you genuinely respect, or one thing you once shared.
Then think of one small, low-stakes step toward them: a question about their kids, a recipe, a game you both follow. If you pray, hold them before God; if you don't, simply wish them well.

wordCard.voice: Social friendship. Fratelli Tutti's name for friendship stretched across a whole society, built by dialogue, and the opposite of war. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: peacemakers treat no one as an enemy. Not agreeing, not even liking, just staying at the table. See you tomorrow.
